mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-23.7 to -20.3). This momentum reflects an ongoing recovery in discretionary outings that will persist absent a shock, pushing the next-28-day mean above the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased monotonically over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: If the 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite the observed 3-week upward trend, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 14.0 to 11.7 over four weeks. Once RESIDENTIAL falls below a 12-point threshold, it indicates households are spending materially less time at home, which mechanically frees time for retail and recreation trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dropped from 14.0 to 11.7 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 2 weeks after RESIDENTIAL crosses below 12.0, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward without a corresponding RETAIL_REC decline, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES (-17.7 to -10.9) and TRANSIT (-30.9 to -24.7) are both recovering simultaneously. Their joint recovery indicates restored commuting and transit-linked foot traffic, which compounds to increase incidental retail visits near transit hubs and workplaces more than either series alone would predict, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved each week over the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over 4 weeks despite continued joint improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, or if the combined effect is no larger than either single-series effect, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery from -30.9 to -24.7 serves as a proxy for loosened mobility restrictions. In a reopening policy regime, continued TRANSIT improvement signals that retail and recreation venues remain open and accessible, driving a further rise in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved by over 6 points across the 4-week window
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to improve but RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines over the next 2 weeks, or if the relationship is only observed because the regime is actually tightening (TRANSIT improvement coincidental), the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows volatile week-to-week swings (-10.6, -9.3, -12.6, -8.3) consistent with short-term weather-driven outdoor activity substitution. When PARKS visits spike upward in a given week, some retail trips are deferred in favor of outdoor recreation, producing a short-horizon dip in RETAIL_REC the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -12.6 to -8.3 in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a PARKS spike greater than 3 points, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has steadily approached baseline, moving from -17.7 to -10.9. Once WORKPLACES crosses above -10 (i.e., within 10 points of baseline), it signals a policy-driven reopening threshold has been crossed, after which retail foot traffic tied to daytime commerce accelerates upward over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -10.9 in the most recent week, nearing the -10 threshold
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES crosses above -10.0 but RETAIL_REC does not show a sustained rise over the subsequent four weeks, the threshold hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility, after improving from -7.1 to -4.3, reflects reduced precautionary stockpiling behavior. If GROCERY_PHARM reverses and worsens by more than 2 points week-on-week, it signals renewed caution among consumers that will also suppress discretionary RETAIL_REC visits within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM worsens by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fluctuated between -7.1 and -4.3 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM worsens by more than 2 points but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, the behavioral caution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT improvement and RESIDENTIAL decline are occurring together, indicating people are both leaving home more and using transit more. This joint shift suggests restored multi-stop daily routines (commute plus errands), which together amplify RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either trend alone would produce over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose and RESIDENTIAL fell concurrently across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks is no greater than what is predicted by TRANSIT or RESIDENTIAL individually, or RETAIL_REC fails to rise despite both trends continuing, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
